ctx.x: Then we have, "The Fabulous Dorseys," 1947, 87 minutes, directed by Alfred E. Green. Dull cliche biography of the two brothers played by themselves with a weighty selection of musical items from their repertoire, including, "Marie," "Green Eyes," "Never Say Never," "The Object of My Affections," and "Dorothy Concerto," by Leo Schuken, and Ray Bauduc. Both the Jimmy Dorsey Orchestra and the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra, with Alvin Stoller on drums, appear with guests Ray Eberle, Stuart Foster, Mike Pingatore, Helen…

Oh, yeah. It was a nightclub scene, and at that time the Old Grey Fox, was what we used to call Tommy then, was on the wagon. He wasn't drinking. But everybody else was. All the booze on the tables in the nightclub scene was real. And we had a delightful time there.
